narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Innaby originated in Azerbaijan as a folk dance for young women.

By the early 20th century, it was firmly established as an 'everyday life dance,' meaning it was integrated into the daily social fabric rather than being reserved solely for the stage or elite courts.
on_screen: Map: Azerbaijan · Central Asia
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: It is a celebratory dance used to mark significant life events like weddings and communal holidays.
It represents the social participation of young women in Azerbaijani cultural life.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by young women and girls.
The motions are characterized as slow and quiet, even though the musical pace is moderately lively.
It is performed in a 6/8 time signature, which typically involves a swaying or skipping feel in Azerbaijani folk traditions.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (QYtzcCP8lLg)
Signature moves — MISSING
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is accompanied by a sazandars ensemble.
Key instruments include the tar (a lute), the kamancha (a bowed string instrument), and the daf (a frame drum).
Listen for the Tar, Kamancha, Daf.
The pulse is 6/8.
The sound is dominated by the plucked resonance of the tar and the melodic wail of the kamancha, underpinned by the steady, driving 6/8 beat of the daf frame drum.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Innaby (Azerbaijan). Meter 6/8. Rhythm pattern: Standard Azerbaijani 6/8 folk rhythm. Instruments: Tar, Kamancha, Daf. Form: Sazandars ensemble performance. Mood: lively, graceful, festive, quiet. It should sound like this: The sound is dominated by the plucked resonance of the tar and the melodic wail of the kamancha, underpinned by the steady, driving 6/8 beat of the daf frame drum.
